reason: 'Thickly textured' leaves, sepals and flowers are thick in substance. PATO_0000591 increased thickness (synonyms thickened, stout) is the existing term; 'textured' adds no separate texture value.
French 'rampant(e)' on rhizomes, stems and whole plants means creeping along the ground. That is FLOPO:0991009 creeping (synonym repent).
'Erectopatent' means between erect (PATO_0000622) and spreading (PATO_0104356). It is a continuum of two existing values, not a new quality.
'Monospermous' means one-seeded: a count of 1 of seed (PO_0009010), and 'seeded' is already in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv.
'Biserial' (French 'bisérié') means arranged in two rows or series, which is FLOPO:0991089 biseriate.

label: bipinnatipartite
definition: A pinnatipartite quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's pinnately parted segments being themselves pinnately parted.
reason: This is a common term for dissected leaves and sepals. It follows FLOPO:0991156 pinnatipartite in the same way that FLOPO:0991014 bipinnate follows pinnate.
In floras, 'wanting' means absent: 'ray-flowers usually wanting', 'the first scale wanting'. The part being described is the part that is absent.

label: cladautoicous
definition: An autoicous quality inhering in a moss plant by virtue of its antheridia being borne on a separate short branch of the same plant that bears the archegonia.
reason: This is a standard moss sexual condition and a kind of autoicous (FLOPO:0991093). Neither PATO nor FLOPO has it.

label: rhizome-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a rhizome: an elongate, horizontal, usually subterranean axis.
reason: It applies to stems, branches, caudices and pseudobulbs. It is worded like the existing -like classes, such as FLOPO:0991142 spike-like and PATO:0002457 leaf-like.
'Alar region distinctly delimited' means clearly set off and visible. This follows the earlier rule that 'distinct' veins are conspicuous, and 'not delimited' is the negated reading.

label: panduriform
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being fiddle-shaped: oblong to obovate, with a concave narrowing on each side below the middle.
reason: It is used for banner petals, petals and bracts. PATO has no violin or fiddle shape, and FLOPO:0991057 lyrate is a different, lobed shape.

label: pleiochasial
definition: A branched quality inhering in a cymose inflorescence by virtue of more than two lateral branches arising below each terminal flower.
reason: This is a standard cyme type. PATO has nothing for it, and FLOPO has only FLOPO:0991179 scorpioid among cyme forms.
'Hoodlike' means hood-shaped, which is FLOPO:0991119 cucullate (synonyms hooded, hood-shaped). 'Not hoodlike' is its negation.
This is a length measurement of trichome (PO_0000282) on the named organ, not a quality word. The whole organ is given by docs/odp/12-part-of-qualified-whole.md.
'Sub-' marks an approximate value of spreading (PATO_0104356), the case the approximate-value pattern covers (as in 'suborbicular').
It means slightly elongated: a weak degree of elongated (PATO_0001154) for moss cells and rootstocks, not a separate quality.
It is the negation of the existing FLOPO:0991063 imbricate ('ni imbriquées' in French).
'Nigrescent' means blackish or turning black. When it says 'when dry' ('à sec'), docs/odp/06-specimen-condition.md applies; 'later/maturing nigrescent' is a stage.
These are the same two words in the other order (French 'pubescent-glanduleux'): FLOPO:0991173 glandular-pubescent.

label: accumbent
definition: A positional quality inhering in a cotyledon by virtue of the cotyledon's edges lying against the radicle, which is folded along them.
reason: This is a standard seed character, chiefly of Brassicaceae, and the opposite of incumbent. The rarer use for filaments lying against grooves is relational and is left out.
'Bridged at 0.2 mm' is a group-specific description of how scales join, given with a height. Without context it is unclear what joins to what.
These statements compare a part's size with another part ('plus court que la corolle', '⅔ des sépales'). Comparisons without a ratio go to docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md.
It means 'callus absent', but there is no usable callus class: PO_0005052 plant callus is culture tissue, and 'callus' was rejected as a generic part in the previous review.
It means 'appendage absent', but 'appendage' was rejected as a generic part in the previous review, and there is no class whose absence could be stated.
'Estipitate' utricles and fruits are not stalked: the negation of FLOPO:0991065 stipitate.
'Bract not sheathed' means it does not sheathe the axis: the negation of FLOPO:0991105 sheathing. The spine example ('neither sheathed nor barbed') is weaker.

label: catadromous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a division of a fern leaf by virtue of the first segment or vein of the division arising on its basiscopic side, towards the base of the axis that bears it.
reason: This is a standard fern character with an opposite, anadromous. Neither PATO nor FLOPO has either.
This is a compound of two values: square (PATO_0000413) with rounded corners, the same as 'oblong-ovate'.
'À bord droit' is straight (PATO_0002180) said of the margin of the disc or petiole. The quality belongs to the margin, a part of the described organ.

label: ancipitous
definition: A flattened quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being compressed so that it has two opposite sharp or narrowly winged edges.
reason: It is common for stems and scapes (Cyperaceae, Iridaceae, orchids). PATO has only flattened, with no term for the two-edged form.
